label: Figure 11.6: The movement from short-run losses to long-run normal profit
alt: Losses cause exit: industry supply shifts left from S to S1, price rises from P to P1, and each remaining firm's demand line rises until it touches the minimum of AC at output q1, where price equals average cost.
caption: In the short run the firm makes the shaded loss at price P and output q. Losses drive firms out, so industry supply shifts left from S to S<sub>1</sub>, raising the price to P<sub>1</sub> and cutting industry output to Q<sub>1</sub>. The firm’s demand line rises to D<sub>1</sub> = AR<sub>1</sub> = MR<sub>1</sub>, which touches the bottom of AC where MC = MR at q<sub>1</sub>; P<sub>1</sub> = C<sub>1</sub> and the loss disappears.
